page: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-96GB is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is configured with a shared CPU allocation model and provides 96.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics. It also achieves top-tier results in software compilation with Clang, image processing, and text processing. Memory bandwidth is strong, ranking in the top 25% for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. However, Passmark memory scores fall into the average category.

The hardware profile presents specific performance tradeoffs. While prompt processing for small LLM models is in the top tier, text generation for the same model is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Additionally, the shared CPU allocation model may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-tenant loads. Qualitatively, the server offers high compute density relative to its memory footprint, making it cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory allocations.

This server is suitable for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and database operations. It is also aligned with batch processing, cryptography, and vector-accelerated workloads utilizing its AVX-512 instruction set.
